extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (registered patent agents and attorneys) and third parties considering filings in published U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and professional-ethics standards governing third‑party submissions of patents/publications in another person's published U.S. patent application, and the disciplinary consequences for noncompliance. Covers timing, content, procedural, and conduct requirements under 37 C.F.R. and the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted time window for third‑party submissions (37 C.F.R. § 1.99)
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party is permitted to submit patents and publications in another person's published application within two months of the date of publication of the application or prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance, whichever is earlier. See 37 C.F.R. § 1.99; see also 35 U.S.C. § 122(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions outside that time period are not permitted unless the applicant consents or other narrow exceptions apply. The MPEP § 1134.01 provides further procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submissions require satisfactory justification (37 C.F.R. § 1.99(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission by a third party beyond the time limits set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 1.99 is permitted only with the applicant's consent or upon a showing that the patents or publications could not have been submitted to the USPTO earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission must include a satisfactory explanation why the patents/publications could not reasonably have been anticipated or submitted during the two‑month window; vague statements (e.g., merely saying the submission responds to a later interview summary) are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions for third‑party submissions (37 C.F.R. § 1.99(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 C.F.R. § 1.99 shall not include any explanation of the patents or publications or any other information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights, markings, annotations, or any explanatory commentary are prohibited (see MPEP § 1134.01, 'Contents Requirements for a Third-party Submission'). Inclusion of such material is grounds for the Office to discard the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No annotations, markings, or explanatory material in submitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights, markings, annotations, underscoring, and any written notations in margins are prohibited in third‑party submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated or marked documents may be discarded and reflect noncompliance with § 1.99 and MPEP § 1134.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, fee, and copy-to-applicant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party submissions must meet procedural requirements such as being signed, paying the requisite fee, and providing a copy to the applicant (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to sign the submission, to pay the fee, or to provide required copies can result in the Office discarding the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party involvement ends at filing; no further contact with the Office (MPEP § 1134.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The involvement of a third party ends with the filing of the submission, and the third party should not contact the Office or submit any other inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated calls or communications with the examiner about the submission or application are inappropriate and may lead to disciplinary referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using PAIR monitoring to justify out‑of‑time filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring the examination on the USPTO's public Patent Application Information Retrieval (PAIR) system does not authorize a third party to file prior art outside the permitted time window simply because the third party 'subjectively came upon information' while monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subjective belief that information encountered on PAIR justifies an out‑of‑time submission is not a valid legal basis for submission under § 1.99.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing/authorization: third parties must have applicant consent or proper standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third‑party submission beyond the permitted limits is allowed only with the applicant's consent; filings on behalf of a party having no standing or not otherwise authorized are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing on behalf of someone who lacks standing (or without required authorization) may be treated as a submission for an improper purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper purpose prohibition (37 C.F.R. § 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO considers the filing of a petition or other paper on behalf of a party having no standing in an application, and not otherwise authorized by the patent rules of practice, to be a petition or paper presented for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers submitted for improper purpose may be subject to disciplinary referral under the Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct standard and disciplinary violation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office (e.g., making third‑party submissions that do not comply with § 1.99) violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such violations can form the basis for disciplinary proceedings and sanctions against the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to OED and potential disciplinary actions for noncompliant filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings by a third party in published applications other than those expressly permitted under 37 C.F.R. § 1.99 may be referred to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) for appropriate disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated or egregious noncompliance (e.g., multiple out‑of‑time filings, annotated submissions, improper contact with examiner) increases the likelihood of OED referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible sanctions and publicity (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26, 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary remedies may include public reprimand, publication of the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette, and notice of discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts in jurisdictions where the practitioner is admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disciplinary record may be considered in future proceedings as an aggravating factor; orders typically specify publication and notice procedures and may address costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement/Final Order procedure for disciplinary matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement that satisfies 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 may resolve a disciplinary complaint by stipulating facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions, subject to approval by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order will set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed discipline, and may preserve the Office's right to consider the record in future matters.
